claims.content: To enable the VMU to investigate and clear conspicuous claims as part of the monitoring system.

goal.raw_text: To enable the VMU to investigate and clear conspicuous claims as part of the monitoring system.

claims.content: VMU User
The data from the forms is entered into a computer database.
Data checks and plausibilisations are done.
The system has provisions for user access controls, including granular model settings.
A claim is entered into the system and undergoes data checks and plausibilisations, resulting in a conspicuous status requiring investigation by the VMU.

trigger.raw_text: A claim is entered into the system and undergoes data checks and plausibilisations, resulting in a conspicuous status requiring investigation by the VMU.

claims.content: The VMU User accesses the system to review claims that have been flagged as conspicuous following data checks and plausibilisations.

The system displays master information for the claim, including Submitted Date, VSP Name, Voucher No, Visit Count, Patient Type, Patient Name, Age, Gender, Address, Contact No, Doctor Name, Doctors Note, HIV Details if any, Patient Status, Claim Amount, and Claim Status.
The VMU User reviews transaction details of the claim, which may include information related to first-time consultation or other service provisions.

The VMU User utilizes reference masters such as Drugs Master, Syndrome Master, Clinical Examination Master, Diagnosis Master, Lab Test Master, Other Measure Master, Patient Status Master, and Claim Status Master to validate and understand the claim components.
Based on the review, the VMU User determines whether the claim is legitimate or requires further action, in alignment with the system’s function to control fraud and ensure timely payments.
If the claim is cleared, the system updates the Claim Status accordingly; if not, it remains under investigation or is escalated per monitoring protocols.

If the VMU User attempts to access a claim without appropriate access level controls or organizational user settings, the system denies access due to high intrusion controls and granular model setting enforcement.

If during review, the system detects missing or invalid master data (e.g., undefined Drug Code, Syndrome Code, or Claim Status Code), it flags the claim as incomplete and prevents clearance until corrected.
If the VMU User identifies fraudulent activity during investigation, the claim is not cleared; instead, it remains under investigation per the monitoring system’s protocol for conspicuous claims.
If database integrity issues occur (e.g., empty unused spaced blocked records or defragmentation failure), the system may halt claim status updates until storage efficiency is restored.
The Claim Status is updated to reflect the outcome of the VMU User’s review (e.g., cleared, under investigation, or escalated).
If the claim is cleared, it becomes eligible for reimbursement via bank transfer as part of the clean claims process.
The system maintains a record of the reviewed claim status within the Claim Status Master for future reference and reporting.
The monitoring system continues to track the voucher scheme’s proper operation through follow-up with patients if required by the review outcome.
